answer: Proof-of-replication storage makes each seat hold its own 50 GB sealed copy of a public archive, for example survey photos of one island's willow wetlands, encoded slowly under that seat's key so two seats can never share a copy. Sealing takes about 6 hours per replica, and each epoch random spot checks demand a few sealed sectors within 2 seconds. A 1,000-persona farm needs about 50 TB of distinct disk, with no ledge where the per-fake cost levels off. Resealing from one master copy on demand fails, since hours of sealing miss a seconds-long deadline.
